text:
jamie_support: Hey team, ACME flagged a big batch job getting a huge number of 429s on /v1/embeddings. They said it was steady after ~150k vectors. Can someone triage?

acme_dataeng: Confirmed — job is sending many concurrent requests from our worker pool. We see 429 body {"error":"rate limit exceeded"} and header X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. Happens after ~10m.

ella_sre: @jamie_support can you paste their request pattern? single requests per vector or batch calls?

jamie_support: They sent batches of 128 vectors with dims 1536 using /v1/embeddings. Example curl from customer below.

acme_dataeng: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"embed-ada-1536","input":[... 128 items ...]}'
```

priya_eng: 128 seems high but should be ok if they respect concurrency. Are they doing many parallel batches?

acme_dataeng: Yes — 40 workers in parallel each sending batch=128, roughly 5120 vectors/sec. They ramped up quickly.

mike_infra: That concurrency definitely could hit per-account token/burst limits. We have a token-bucket ratecap that is per-customer and has a burst window. If too many parallel requests, Remaining header can drop to 0.

ella_sre: Do we have logs for their API key around the timestamps? @mike_infra can you check gateway logs for 1891234500-1891234600 range?

mike_infra: Pulling logs now... deploy-bot: logs retrieved for key=acct_XXXX, 1891234498-1891234630. Notable: ~1600 req/min at peak, many 429 responses with header Retry-After: 3.

jamie_support: They reported intermittent dimension mismatch errors earlier — "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 0" — any relation?

priya_eng: That sounds like malformed payloads (empty string or a None) coming from their ingestion pipeline. Those wouldn't cause 429s though. Could be separate. Ask them to validate input lengths.

acme_dataeng: We do have a few job errors where some items were empty; we filtered those now. But 429s continued.

ella_sre: Two avenues: 1) show them how to reduce concurrency and add exponential backoff with jitter; 2) check server-side throttling and see if we can offer temporary elevated burst for a big migration.

jamie_support: Customer asked for immediate workaround while we investigate. Priya, can you paste a recommended backoff snippet?

priya_eng: Sure — recommend exponential backoff + full jitter and limit in-flight requests. Example pseudocode: 

```
maxConcurrent = 8
for batch in batches:
  wait_for_slot(maxConcurrent)
  attempt = 0
  while attempt < 6:
    resp = send_batch(batch)
    if resp.status == 200: break
    if resp.status == 429 or resp.status == 503:
      sleep = random_uniform(0, (2 ** attempt) * base_ms) / 1000
      sleep_seconds(sleep)
      attempt += 1
    else: raise error
```

priya_eng: Also check Retry-After header and back off at least that amount.

acme_dataeng: We'll try lowering concurrency to 8 and implement jittered backoff. Trying now.

mike_infra: On infra side I see that their bursts were exhausting the short-term bucket. We can temporarily increase their burst window for a migration if they sign a short ticket. But policy requires confirmation.

jamie_support: @acme_dataeng are you asking for a temporary bump or do you want to test with backoff first?

acme_dataeng: We'll test backoff first. If that still doesn't meet their SLA for the migration we'll ask for a temporary bump.

ella_sre: While they test, @mike_infra can you also check whether their requests were hitting multiple model variants or a fallback that might be slower? Sometimes routing to a larger-sequence variant drops throughput.

mike_infra: Checked — all requests routed to embed-ada-1536 in prod; no fallbacks observed. Latency was within expected ranges (p50 40ms, p95 200ms at low load). At peak we saw queueing spikes to ~900ms which increases concurrency footprint.

priya_eng: Another optimization: increase batch size to 256 if each vector is small and you have headroom in model memory — that reduces request rate. But only if you can limit concurrency. Batch-vs-concurrency tradeoff.

acme_dataeng: We'll try: batch 256 with concurrency 4 vs batch 128 concurrency 8 and report which finishes faster w/ fewer 429s.

jamie_support: For reproducibility — please capture a short HAR or a few example request IDs when you see 429s and paste here. We can correlate to logs.

acme_dataeng: Provided three request IDs: req_85812, req_85813, req_85814 at 1891234512-1891234520.

mike_infra: Correlated: those map to gateway shards A3 and A4 showing Returned 429, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 3. Also note they sent several malformed empty inputs earlier which caused retries from their client — that increased effective request rate.

ella_sre: Action items: 1) @acme_dataeng — implement backoff + reduce concurrency, run perf test and report. 2) @mike_infra — evaluate temporary burst increase procedure and estimate impact. 3) @priay_eng — share sample backoff code and batching guidance (done). 4) @jamie_support — follow up on customer's ask for migration window if they choose bump.

jamie_support: Noted. ACME will try now and update within 30m. If they still need a bump I'll open a ticket for manual adjustment.

acme_dataeng: Update: reduced concurrency -> 6, added jitter backoff; after 20m no 429s so far, overall throughput reduced ~35% but job completed without failure. Thanks.

ella_sre: Great. @mike_infra please draft a safe bump playbook in case they request one later (limits, duration, rollback).

mike_infra: Will do. Also adding a note to monitor malformed inputs — we should add a quick client-side validation snippet to our docs for embeddings to reduce accidental empty vectors.

jamie_support: Closing loop once ACME confirms full migration done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
